description: Project PLATEAU, led by Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism with many partners, builds and publishes 3D city models of Japanese cities as open data, as digital infrastructure for digital transformation in urban planning. Models of more than 250 cities are available through the G-Spatial Information Center. They follow a format based on the CityGML standard and are semantic models: buildings, roads and other objects carry attributes such as usage, year of construction and urban planning data. Since March 2021 PLATEAU has maintained Japan's Standard Data Product Specification for 3D City Models, now at version 5.0, unifying specifications, formats and quality requirements; it offers handbooks, use cases, technical reports, the PLATEAU VIEW viewer and code. Coverage: 250-plus Japanese cities. Access: open data downloads and viewers from the PLATEAU and G-Spatial Information Center sites. Licence: open data; the terms were not read on the day. Caveats: attribute richness and level of detail differ between cities and years. Simulation uses are city digital twins for disaster preparedness, including earthquake and heavy rainfall, energy and urban planning. Related records: the OGC CityGML standard.
